description:
The surah that opens with the oath of the Divine One swearing by **The Wresters**, the angelic pullers, who shall harshly wrest out the souls of the unbelievers at their appointed time of death. It takes its name from "the wresters" (al-nāziʿāt) mentioned in verse 1. The main theme of the surah is the possibility and inevitability of the Resurrection, its results, and its timing. The story of Moses and Pharaoh acts as encouragement to the Prophet and a warning to the disbelievers.
The surah is also known as (Soul-)Snatchers, Extractors, The Angelic Pullers, The Forceful Chargers, The Pluckers, The Soul-Snatchers, Those That Rise, Those Who Pull and Withdraw, Those Who Tear Out

7.1: Apparently, 'the Quaker' and 'the Successor' refer to the first and the second blasts of the Trumpet sounded by Isrāfīl on the Day of Resurrection. Cf. <{["Q", "39:68"]}>; <{["Q", "73:14"]}>.

translations.1: By those [angels] who wrest [the soul] violently,
translations.2: by those who draw [it] out gently,
translations.4: by those who take the lead, racing,
translations.5: by those who direct the affairs [of creatures]:
translations.6: the day when the Quaker quakes
translations.7: and is followed by the Successor,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.8: hearts will be trembling on that day,
translations.10:
They will say,
  'Are we being returned to our earlier state?
translations.11: What, when we have been decayed bones?!'
translations.12: They will say, 'This, then, is a ruinous return!'
translations.13: Yet it will be only a single shout,
translations.14: and behold, they will be awake.
translations.15: Did you receive the story of Moses,
translations.16:
when his Lord called out to him
   in the holy valley of Ṭuwā?
translations.17:
[And said,] 'Go to Pharaoh,
  for indeed he has rebelled,
translations.19:
I will guide you to your Lord,
   that you may fear [Him]?" '
translations.20: Then he showed him the greatest sign.
translations.22: Then he turned back, walking swiftly,
translations.25:
So Allah seized him
  with the punishment of this life and the Hereafter.
translations.26: There is indeed a moral in that for someone who fears!
translations.27:
Is it you whose creation is more prodigious
  or the sky which He has built?
translations.28: He raised its vault, and fashioned it,
translations.29:
and darkened its night,
  and brought forth its day;
translations.30: and after that He spread out the earth,
translations.31: and brought forth from it its water and pastures,
translations.33:
as a [place of] sustenance for you
   and your livestock.
translations.35: the day when man will remember his endeavours,
translations.36: and hell is brought into view for one who sees,
translations.37: as for him who was rebellious
translations.38: and preferred the life of this world,
translations.39: his refuge will indeed be hell.
translations.40:
But as for him who is awed to stand before his Lord
  and forbids the soul from [following] desire,
translations.41: his refuge will indeed be paradise.
translations.42:
They ask _you_ concerning the Hour,
  "When will it set in,
translations.45: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
translations.46:
The day they see it, it shall be as if
  they had not stayed [in the world]
   except for an evening or forenoon.
